title: Foton and CUBOTECH bring Law and quantum computing together in seminar
summary: A seminar announced for October 9–10, 2026, affiliated with Unisinos, promotes interdisciplinary debate between Law and quantum computing.
body:
## Quantum computing meets Law

Quantum technologies raise challenges that go beyond the traditional fields of physics, mathematics, and computing. Their possible impacts on information security, data protection, digital governance, and technology regulation require dialogue across different research areas.

In this context, the **Instituto Foton and the CUBOTECH — Law and Technology Research Group** announced the **First Research Seminar on Law and Quantum Computing**, presented as an online event for **October 9 and 10, 2026**, affiliated with the **University of Vale do Rio dos Sinos (Unisinos)**.

### An encounter between different fields

The initiative sought to encourage interdisciplinary discussions about the scientific, legal, social, and economic impacts of quantum technologies.

The objectives presented in the program included strengthening research networks, promoting academic exchange, and building knowledge about governance and innovation.

The organizers also planned an **e-book** with academic works related to the seminar, contributing to the circulation of the knowledge discussed. **The actual availability of the publication depends on confirmation of its release.**

### Technology research and social questions

For Instituto Foton, the collaboration with CUBOTECH represents an opportunity to connect different fields of knowledge and broaden the debate about the role of quantum technologies in Brazilian society.

The initiative was publicized externally by the **ON/COMUNG Platform, in a publication linked to Unisinos on August 13, 2026**, and had an official page on the university platform. The published program documents the proposal for the meeting, but it is not a later report on its execution.

**Event dates:** October 9 and 10, 2026.

**Image:** institutional promotional artwork for the First Research Seminar on Law and Quantum Computing; individual creation credit was not provided by the source.

**External publications:**
- [Institutional announcement — ON/COMUNG Platform](https://comung.comunitarias.org.br/unisinos/noticias/primeiro-seminario-de-pesquisa-cubotech-e-instituto-de-ciencia-e-tecnologias-quanticas-foton.html)
- [Official seminar page — Unisinos](https://eventos.unisinos.br/primeiroseminariocubotech/)

### Different knowledge, shared questions

The collaboration exemplifies how research into emerging technologies can be enriched by the participation of researchers from other fields, contributing to a broader understanding of their impact on society.

title: Foton connects quantum computing and business at Mobi Festival
summary: The Mobi Festival 2026 announcement details the Mobi Quantum curation, with discussions on innovation, digital security, talent, and the National Quantum Manifesto.
body:
## Quantum technologies in dialogue with business and society

The **Mobi Festival 2026**, scheduled for **June 11–13** at the University of Sorocaba (Uniso), included **Mobi Quantum** in its published agenda, a forum dedicated to the relationship between quantum technologies, business, and innovation. According to institutional communication published on June 9, **Instituto Foton** acted as co-organizer alongside **Uniso and Unisotech**, taking responsibility for organizing and curating the quantum track.

The announced program brought together specialists, researchers, entrepreneurs, technology professionals, and institutional representatives to discuss **digital security, cryptography, business applications, smart cities, and talent development**.

### Mobi Quantum, HaQuantum, and the Manifesto

The announcement described panels and workshops on technological transition and market challenges. The agenda also included presentations and training activities intended to make quantum computing more accessible to people from different fields.

**HaQuantum**, promoted by Instituto Foton in partnership with the **Uniso Academic League of Quantum Computing**, was presented on its registration page as a journey with preparatory meetings and quantum optimization challenges, culminating in presentations by finalist teams planned for the festival.

Another announced initiative was the presentation of the **first stage of the National Quantum Manifesto**, a proposal to bring together researchers, companies, public institutions, and civil society around priorities for Brazilian technological development.

### What the sources actually confirm

The sources consulted include an **announcement published before the festival** and a **HaQuantum program page**. Therefore, the panels, presentations, and objectives described here correspond to what was **announced**; they are not presented as verified execution results, participant counts, or later deliverables.

**Festival dates:** June 11–13, 2026. **Location:** University of Sorocaba, São Paulo.

**References:**
- [Instituto Foton — Mobi Quantum program](https://www.ictqfoton.org/post/instituto-foton-leva-computa%C3%A7%C3%A3o-qu%C3%A2ntica-aplicada-a-neg%C3%B3cios-ao-mobi-festival-2026)
- [Even3 — HaQuantum](https://www.even3.com.br/e/hackathon-quantum-731810)

title: Instituto Foton and Gravataí document an innovation partnership
summary: A record published on May 22, 2026 describes cooperation to raise awareness and coordinate the innovation ecosystem, with no financial transfer planned.
body:
## An agreement to foster ecosystem connections

A record published on **May 22, 2026** by the **National Public Procurement Portal (PNCP)** documents the partnership agreement between the **Municipality of Gravataí, Rio Grande do Sul**, and the **Instituto de Ciências e Tecnologias Quânticas Foton**.

The record describes cooperative activities focused on **raising awareness, coordinating, and integrating the innovation and emerging-technology ecosystem**. It references Article 9 of **Law No. 10,973/2004** and a work plan associated with the partnership.

### Institutional cooperation without claiming undocumented results

The document states that the partnership **has no financial link and creates no expense for the Municipality**. The formal amount of R$0.01 shown in the procurement record should not be interpreted as research investment or a transfer of resources to the Institute.

The public record supports the existence of the institutional coordination and its planned scope, but by itself it does not demonstrate that events, programs, or projects were executed. Any concrete result should be reported separately once documentary evidence is available.

### Reference for consultation

**Record publication date:** May 22, 2026. **Location:** Gravataí, Rio Grande do Sul.

**PNCP identifier:** 87890992000158-1-000469/2026. **Process:** 170/2026. **Reference:** Direct award 24/2026.

The partnership signals a shared intention to bring institutions, people, and innovation initiatives closer together, while preserving the distinction between **formalization** and **deliverables actually documented**.

**Public consultation:** [Partnership agreement record — LicitaPNCP](https://licitapncp.com.br/licitacao/acordo-de-parceria-com-o-instituto-foton-com-base-no-art-9-da-lei-n-10-87890992000158-1-000469-2026).

title: Uniso Quantum Day highlights the delivery of the Leonti Project
summary: The April 7, 2026 meeting brought together education, research, and innovation and presented the Leonti photonic prototype to LACQ Uniso.
body:
## Research and scientific training in the same meeting

On **April 7, 2026**, the University of Sorocaba (Uniso) held the first edition of **Uniso Quantum Day**, bringing together students, researchers, and technology-sector representatives. The program discussed scientific training, applications of quantum technologies, and closer ties between the university and innovation.

The event concluded with the delivery ceremony for the **Leonti Project** to the Uniso Academic League of Quantum Computing. Coverage by **Agência Focas/Uniso** describes the equipment as a **photonic quantum-computer prototype**, developed within the institution's engineering environment and presented to the public during the event.

### A project built with different skills

According to the report, the project began in 2024 and is linked to collaboration between Uniso and **Q-Bra (Qubits Brasil)**, a startup founded by **Samuel Rufino**, who is also connected to ICT Unisotech. The article identifies **Denicezar Angelo Baldo** as coordinator of Uniso's Computer Engineering program and a member of the project team. **Wilson Fonseca** and **Alessandro de Oliveira Faria** are cited as developers of the **DiraQ** operating system. The coverage also recognizes the participation of Nilo Koscheck Chagas, Vitor Gabriel, and Luís Roberto Momberg Albano.

These roles are presented according to the source's attribution, without assuming additional responsibilities. **Displaying a prototype does not, by itself, prove computational capacity, qubit count, or operational performance**; the reports consulted do not provide benchmarking results that would support those conclusions.

### Education, creativity, and academic leagues

During Quantum Day, **Rosângela Viegas Maraschin**, presented in the coverage as vice president of Instituto Foton, discussed the challenge of engineering education and the importance of preserving creativity in learning. She also highlighted the role of academic leagues as environments for experimentation and the development of new talent.

The second Agência Focas article, published on April 6, provides context about the prototype's preparation and the participation of Uniso students. Together, the two reports document the project's educational path without replacing the need for independent technical validation of the equipment.

**Event date:** April 7, 2026. **Location:** University of Sorocaba, São Paulo.

**Further reading:**
- [Agência Focas — Leonti Project delivery and Uniso Quantum Day](https://focas.uniso.br/index.php/2026/04/09/entrega-do-projeto-leonti-marca-a-primeira-edicao-do-uniso-quantum-day/)
- [Agência Focas — Prototype development at Uniso](https://focas.uniso.br/index.php/2026/04/06/alunos-da-uniso-desenvolvem-primeiro-computador-quantico-da-regiao-metropolitana-de-sorocaba/)

title: Instituto Foton and Assespro-RS expand connections with the technology sector
summary: A cooperation agreement signed on August 22, 2025 provides for research, technological development, and professional training initiatives.
body:
## Bringing research and the productive sector closer

On **August 22, 2025**, Instituto Foton expanded its connections with the technology sector by formalizing a **Cooperation Agreement with Assespro-RS**.

The agreement was signed by **Leonardo Camargo Rossato**, president of Instituto Foton, and **Alexandre Mello**, president of Assespro-RS, during a meeting of the association's board.

The collaboration covers research projects, technological development, and professional training, as well as actions intended to integrate companies, startups, and educational institutions.

### Different skills, shared interests

The development of quantum technologies involves diverse skills. Universities and research centers contribute scientific knowledge, while the productive sector brings technological challenges and opportunities for application.

Encouraging dialogue between these environments can help identify shared interests, train professionals, and build collaborative projects.

For Instituto Foton, cooperation with Assespro-RS represents an initiative to coordinate science, technology, and entrepreneurship.

### The documented partnership

The Cooperation Agreement was **officially reported by Assespro-RS on August 26, 2025**, in a publication documenting the signing and presenting the partnership's institutional objectives.

The record also demonstrates Instituto Foton's presence in Rio Grande do Sul's innovation ecosystem, the state where the organization was founded.

**Agreement date:** August 22, 2025.

**Photographic record:** partnership between Instituto Foton and Assespro-RS.

**External publication:** [Assespro-RS signs Cooperation Agreement with Instituto Fóton+](https://www.assespro-rs.org.br/post-acontece/assespro-rs-assina-termo-de-coopera%C3%A7%C3%A3o-com-o-instituto-f%C3%B3ton).

title: Instituto Foton takes part in the launch of LACQ PUCRS
summary: The April 16, 2025 program at Tecnopuc brought the academic community closer to discussions about quantum technologies.
body:
## An academic league bringing people and research together

The launch of the **PUCRS Academic League of Quantum Computing (LACQ PUCRS)** was announced for **April 16, 2025**, at Tecnopuc in Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul. The initiative emerged from the mobilization of university students and professors, with support from **LACQ Feynman** and **Instituto Foton**.

According to the published program, the meeting sought to bring together students, researchers, and people interested in the scientific, social, and economic applications of quantum technologies. The Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, the Polytechnic School, and Tecnopuc were among the organizers.

### Accessible knowledge and talent development

**Leonardo Rossato**, president of Instituto Foton, was included in the announced program with the talk **“Introduction to quantum technologies and their social and economic impacts.”** The schedule also included presentations about LACQ Feynman and LACQ UFRGS by Gabriel Albuquerque and Natan Tristão, as well as an institutional presentation about Foton.

The meeting illustrates the importance of academic leagues in connecting university education, science communication, and innovation ecosystems. For Foton, strengthening these connections is a way to broaden the participation of new talent in an interdisciplinary field.

### Record and context

The **Brasil Inovador** article, published on April 16, 2025, presents the location, partners, and program. It is an event announcement; by itself, it is not a report of results achieved later.

**Program date:** April 16, 2025. **Location:** Pitch Stage, Tecnopuc, Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul.

**Reference:** [Brasil Inovador — launch of LACQ PUCRS](https://brasilinovador.com.br/lancamento-da-liga-academica-de-computacao-quantica-da-pucrs-no-dia-16-04-25/).

title: Instituto Foton and SOFTSUL establish cooperation in quantum technologies
summary: An agreement signed on March 19, 2025 establishes a basis for research, technological development, and training in quantum computing.
body:
## Cooperation to develop quantum-technology skills

On **March 19, 2025**, Instituto Foton and SOFTSUL formalized a Cooperation Agreement to encourage research, technological development, and training in quantum computing and related fields.

The document was signed by **Leonardo Camargo Rossato**, president of Instituto Foton, and **José Antonio Antonioni**, president of SOFTSUL.

The initiative brings together two institutions interested in strengthening Brazilian capabilities in emerging technologies, recognizing the importance of professional training and collaboration between scientific and business environments.

### Knowledge bringing science and the productive sector together

Quantum computing offers possible applications in different sectors, but its development depends on specialized knowledge, infrastructure, and collaboration networks.

In this context, the agreement establishes an institutional basis for exchanging experience, bringing talent closer, and developing joint initiatives.

For Instituto Foton, this cooperation aligns with the proposal to connect different actors in Brazil's technology ecosystem, creating conditions for scientific research to engage with real-world challenges.

### Institutional record

The signing was reported by **SOFTSUL on its institutional portal on May 5, 2025**, which records the representatives involved and the objectives of the cooperation.

**Agreement date:** March 19, 2025.

**External publication:** [SOFTSUL and Instituto FÓTON+ sign agreement to foster innovation in quantum technologies](https://www.softsul.org.br/softsul-e-instituto-foton-firmam-acordo-para-fomentar-a-inovacao-em-tecnologias-quanticas/).

**Photographic archive:** records made available in Instituto Foton's institutional IMG-News folder.

title: The day Instituto Foton was founded.
summary: On January 30, 2025, a hybrid assembly held in Porto Alegre brought together researchers and professionals from different regions to found Instituto Foton.
body:
## January 30, 2025: the meeting that gave rise to Instituto Foton

**A hybrid assembly brought together researchers and professionals from different regions of Brazil and marked the beginning of a collective effort around quantum technologies.**

### A day to begin a new story

On January 30, 2025, professionals and researchers connected to quantum sciences and technologies met to formally establish Instituto Foton. The meeting took place at NAU Live Spaces in Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, with online participation from other regions of Brazil.

The hybrid format made it possible to bring together people who, even in different places, shared an interest in strengthening connections between science, education, research, and innovation.

### An assembly that connected people

The assembly brought together distinct professional and scientific paths around the creation of an institution dedicated to quantum technologies. The presence of participants both on site and online marked the collaborative dimension of the initiative from its formation.

### Institutional formation

The meeting also had a formal character. According to the founding minutes, the Social Statute was presented and discussed, followed by its unanimous approval. The first Executive Board was elected at the assembly, completing the institutional procedures for establishing the Institute.

This historical composition should be distinguished from the people who currently hold institutional roles. The photograph of the first board records the founding moment, not the Institute's current structure.

### The people behind the foundation

The assembly records preserve the participation of founders and collaborators. Among the people identified in the third archive card is Gabriel Albuquerque, present as president of LACQ Feynman, a sister institution: **he was not part of Foton's statutory board**. The complete identification of the people photographed accompanies the corresponding image in the gallery below.

### The beginning of a collective effort

The formal establishment created an institutional basis for coordinating research, talent development, connections between institutions, and the development of quantum technologies. These directions represent the purposes that guided the creation of the Institute; they should not be confused with results already achieved at that assembly.

### A story that continues

The foundation is the first chapter of work built through the contributions of people from different fields and regions of the country. Instituto Foton continues this path with a commitment to bringing knowledge closer and creating opportunities for scientific collaboration.

**Date:** January 30, 2025 · **Location:** NAU Live Spaces, Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, with online participation.
